Date: 2025-09-30

Duration: 68 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sara Li (Redwood SE) | Priya Nair (CTO, Polaris), Omar Ruiz (Head ML Infra), Linda Gomez (IT Ops), Samir Patel (SRE)

transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We have about an hour, hour ten. quick intro, I'm Maya, will coordinate the pilot. Ethan and Sara from SE will drive the technical pieces. Priya, Omar, Linda, Samir from Polaris, welcome.

[00:22] Priya (CTO): Thanks Maya, yep we ran the pre-call checklist. main thing for us is air-gapped delivery and license activation, we can't have egress from the cluster once artifacts land.

[00:40] Ethan (SE): Totally makes sense. we'll walk through two patterns: sealed bundle (signed tar on removable media) and side-load via controlled jump host with one-time transfer keys. both support offline license activation.

[01:05] Omar (Head ML Infra): Quick question — for sealed bundle, what's the verification story? we've had manual steps that are error-prone.

[01:22] Sara (SE): Good call. we include a signed manifest with RSA2048 signatures and a SHA256 checksum. the runbook has the exact openssl verify and sha256sum steps; we also provide a small verification utility that runs offline. sometimes the transcripting in our docs says "R S A two oh four eight" — but it's RSA-2048.

[01:45] Linda (IT Ops): And how do we get the keys? we can't take them into the air-gapped zone.

[01:53] Maya (AE): Two options: pre-provisioned license files that you drop in a protected HSM or KMS on a management host, or an activation token we sign and stamp before handoff. both are possible; we recommend HSM-backed key storage for regulated workloads.

[02:20] Samir (SRE): For the activation token, is there any outbound call needed to Redwood? because our security posture forbids outbound once in production.

[02:33] Ethan (SE): No outbound required for the sealed flow. activation tokens include an offline signature that your local service can validate. the only time we call out is if you choose the remote-activation flow for faster rotation, but for air-gapped you use the pre-signed license file.

[02:54] Priya (CTO): Great. now on runtime — our workload is heavy on long context genomics prompts, so KV cache warmup matters. what are your recommended warmup patterns?

[03:12] Ethan (SE): For long-context workloads we strongly recommend prefix caching: run a synthetic warmup that streams typical prefixes to populate the KV cache before traffic hits prod. we provide a warmup harness that replays 1.5x your normal token volume to stabilize the temp GPU memory allocations. note: if you restore from a checkpoint, kv cache state isn't portable across model versions, so plan warmups on each rollout.

[03:47] Omar (Head ML Infra): How long does the warmup take for, say, a 4x A100 cluster?

[03:55] Ethan (SE): Depends on sequence length distribution. with 2k average sequence length, we saw warmup times of 20–45 minutes for a modest cluster. we'll include benchmarking numbers in the runbook. also watch for KV cache fragmentation if you use very heterogeneous request sizes.

[04:24] Linda (IT Ops): On batching — we need predictable p95 latency under 350ms. can we achieve that with batch sizes >1?

[04:36] Sara (SE): You can, with dynamic batching and latency SLOs. the runtime will prioritize low-latency requests but still group others when idle. recommended approach: set a target max latency (300ms), configure max batch size to what the GPU can handle for your model (we'll recommend based on quantization), and enable pro-active batching windows of 10–20ms. for genomics long contexts, you'll likely stay at batch sizes 2–4 to meet p95.

[05:12] Priya (CTO): How does quantization affect accuracy for our models? we can't accept more than 1.5% change in key evaluation metrics.

[05:24] Ethan (SE): We suggest starting with 8-bit quant (q8) using per-channel scales, and running a small eval set. in our internal tests, q8 asymmetric gave <1% drop on similar LLMs for generation tasks; but for sensitive genomics annotation you may want q8-fp4 hybrid or fallback to 16-bit in critical routes. the Redwood Optimize tool can run automated regression checks against your eval prompts.

[05:58] Omar (Head ML Infra): Are there any special kernel modules we need for certain quant backends?

[06:07] Sara (SE): Yes — some optimized kernels rely on CUDA extensions present in the NVIDIA driver >= 535.x and matching cuDNN. we'll provide a driver-compat matrix. if you intend to use our int8 optimized path, we recommend driver 535.86+ and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with kernel 5.15+; we'll include rollback notes.

[06:40] Linda (IT Ops): What about air-gapped installs — how do you deliver the drivers? we usually can't access NVIDIA repos from inside the network.

[06:52] Ethan (SE): We'll provide a driver bundle tar that includes the exact deb/rpm and kernel module installers plus checksums and a small offline installer script. we also include a guide for signing kernel modules if your security team requires module signature.

[07:15] Priya (CTO): We have heterogeneous nodes — some older gen 80GB, others 40GB. does Redwood's runtime handle mixed-memory clusters?

[07:27] Sara (SE): Yes, smart routing will schedule shards by memory fit; however you should pin heavy-request routes to the 80GB class to avoid cross-node transfers. for KV cache heavy scenarios, co-locating cache and compute minimizes cross-host network.

[07:46] Samir (SRE): Do we need RDMA for best performance?

[07:52] Ethan (SE): RDMA helps for model sharding and large KV exchanges, but it's not mandatory. if you have it, throughput and latency improve for cross-node attention patterns. it's worth enabling for multi-node A100 sharded setups.

[08:16] Priya (CTO): Any gotchas with SELinux or AppArmor in the install? last time an agent got blocked by policies.

[08:25] Sara (SE): The offline installer has flags to run in permissive mode and generate a policy template. we recommend generating and vetting the profile first. we'll include suggested policies in the runbook.

[08:40] Maya (AE): Quick pause — I want to flag the pilot acceptance criteria so the team is aligned. Priya, can you confirm success metrics?

[08:52] Priya (CTO): We'll measure p95 latency <350ms for the primary route, sustained throughput of X tokens/sec we shared in the deck, and no data exfiltration. Also 99% successful activation of offline licenses across nodes.

[09:12] Maya (AE): Great. Ethan, could you sketch the pilot steps?

[09:19] Ethan (SE): Sure: 1) Redwood provides signed artifact bundle + driver tar and runbook; 2) Polaris ingests into staging air-gapped cluster using verification utility; 3) run warmup harness for 48h; 4) run synthetic and real traffic for 24h; 5) capture traces and share with Redwood. we will assist remotely during the handoff but won't have network access to your cluster.

[09:55] Omar (Head ML Infra): About traces — are there any PII or genomic sequence strings in logs by default? we need to ensure compliance.

[10:06] Sara (SE): The runtime can redact payloads at token level and you can configure sampling ratios. default telemetry is metrics-only (latency, token counts, mem usage). logs that include request payloads are opt-in and should be disabled in air-gapped production.

[10:28] Priya (CTO): On the signing utility — is that cross-platform? our ops use RHEL and Debian.

[10:36] Ethan (SE): Yes, the verification binary is static and works on RHEL8+, Debian 10+, and we include python fallback. it does not require outbound access.

[10:49] Linda (IT Ops): For the sealed media — any recommendations for physical handoff chain-of-custody? we have a rigorous process.

[10:58] Maya (AE): We recommend tamper-evident packaging, signed manifests, and shared acknowledgement forms. Redwood can pre-sign the manifest and supply an audit log CSV that you append with receiving signatures. we'll provide a template.

[11:20] Samir (SRE): Regarding kernel compat, if a kernel upgrade is needed, will that break our other workloads?

[11:29] Sara (SE): It can. the runbook includes a compatibility matrix and a rollback plan. we typically advise doing a staged upgrade on one non-critical node first.

[11:43] Priya (CTO): Can Redwood provide the driver bundle with extra instrumentation for perf debugging?

[11:51] Ethan (SE): Yes, we can include flamegraphs and perf counters in the build, but those are optional. note that some perf tools require kernel debug symbols which your security team may restrict.

[12:10] Maya (AE): I'm seeing some questions in chat about alternate activation flows — Sara, can you summarize the two secure activation patterns?

[12:19] Sara (SE): Sure: A) Pre-signed license files: we sign license blobs and you drop them into a local KMS/HSM — fully offline. B) One-time activation token: we sign a time-limited token and hand it over physically; the local agent validates it and stores it encrypted. both avoid outbound. option A is easier for rotation via exchange of new files.

[12:46] Omar (Head ML Infra): About model rollouts — if we push a new model, does the offline license need re-issuing?

[12:55] Ethan (SE): No, license is generally per-deployment not per-model; however if you switch to a different Redwood SKU that uses distinct binaries we may require a new license blob. we'll document SKU vs model rules.

[13:12] Priya (CTO): Let's talk perf tuning knobs — where do we start?

[13:20] Sara (SE): Start with three levers: quantization, batching, and kernel selection. quantify accuracy tradeoffs offline, pick safe quant (q8 per-channel), set max batch sizes by GPU mem, and enable the optimized kernel path we include in the driver bundle. also tune prefix cache TTLs so the KV cache doesn't evict hot prefixes too aggressively.

[13:52] Samir (SRE): Does the runtime expose metrics for KV hit rate?

[13:58] Ethan (SE): Yep — hit rate, eviction counts, cache lookups per request, and per-prefix latency. we'll provide Grafana dashboards and the Prometheus scrape config in the runbook.

[14:16] Priya (CTO): Any known issues for mixed-quant clusters? like some nodes running q8 kernels and others q16?

[14:27] Sara (SE): Mixed quant is supported but routing must be quant-aware; we can do automatic fallback if a node can't serve a quantized shard but that adds latency. for production, it's preferable to homogeneous quant classes per pool.

[14:44] Maya (AE): I'm going to read back the immediate deliverables so we all agree. Ethan, driver bundle + sha256 and driver-compat matrix?

[14:52] Ethan (SE): Yes. we'll push a sealed driver bundle with installers for both RPM and DEB, plus the module signature guide. expect to receive by Oct 2.

[15:03] Maya (AE): Maya sends signed artifact checklist and offline runbook?

[15:07] Maya (AE): I'll send the checklist and the runbook by Oct 3.

[15:11] Priya (CTO): We'll confirm hardware list and kernel versions by Oct 1.

[15:15] Omar (Head ML Infra): We'll run the 48-hour warmup in staging and share logs week of Oct 6.

[15:22] Linda (IT Ops): One more question — if we find a driver mismatch, can we request an incremental hotfix bundle or do we need full re-bundle?

[15:31] Sara (SE): We can do incremental hotfixes; our release process supports micro-bundles with checksums. the runbook explains the process.

[15:45] Priya (CTO): Okay. any risks we should flag now?

[15:52] Ethan (SE): Main risk is KV warmup time and cold-start latency on large contexts. mitigation: run warmups, use prefix caching, and have a small pre-warm traffic window during rollout. second risk is kernel module signing policies blocking driver installs; mitigation: generate policy templates and work with your security team.

[16:21] Maya (AE): Great, I'm going to put the action items in the deck and follow up in email. last thing — do you want Redwood to bring a remote engineer to the hands-on day?

[16:30] Priya (CTO): Yes please, one remote SE during the handoff would be helpful.

[16:36] Maya (AE): Noted. we'll include a remote SE support slot for the pilot kickoff.

[16:42] Samir (SRE): Quick nit — can the verification tool produce a machine-readable JSON receipt we can ingest into our CMDB?

[16:49] Ethan (SE): Yes, it emits a JSON receipt with artifact id, sha256, timestamp, and signature. we'll include a sample.

[17:05] Priya (CTO): Perfect. thanks everyone. let's reconvene after the pilot kickoff.

[17:12] Maya (AE): Thanks all. I'll follow up with the checklist and schedule. bye.
notes: Shared artifacts referenced: Polaris-offline-checklist.pdf (customer), redwood-offline-runtime-runbook-v2.pdf (redwood), driver-compat-matrix.xlsx (redwood). Verification utility binary included (static build).
